in_hebrew.name: מילבורגה
in_hebrew.meaning: מילבורגה משמעות שם נוצרי חזק וקדוש
in_hebrew.long_meaning: מילבורגה הוא שם נוצרי שמקורו באנגלית העתיקה, נגזר מהמילים 'מיל' שפירושה 'עושר' ו'בורג' שפירושה 'מבצר' או 'עיר מבוצרת'. הוא משלב את הרעיון של עושר רוחני עם מושג החוזק וההגנה שמציע מבצר. השם עשוי להיות קשור לחוזק רוחני ולעושר פנימי בחיי הנוצרי.

in_greek.name: Μιλβούργα
in_greek.long_meaning: Το όνομα Μιλβούργα προέρχεται από την παλιά αγγλική γλώσσα, συνδυάζοντας τις λέξεις 'μιλ' που σημαίνει 'πλούτος' και 'βούργ' που σημαίνει 'φρούριο' ή 'ενδυναμωμένη πόλη'. Συμβολίζει τον πλούτο της ψυχής και την πνευματική δύναμη που προσφέρει ένα φρούριο προστασίας. Στην παράδοση της Εκκλησίας, το όνομα συνδέεται με την πνευματική ανάπτυξη και την προστασία που προσφέρει ο Θεός.

in_latin.name: Milburga
in_latin.meaning: Fortis et dives, vel opulenta urbs
in_latin.long_meaning: Nomen Milburga ex antiqua lingua Anglica derivatum est, componitur ex 'mil' quod significat 'divitiae' et 'burg' quod est 'urbs munita' vel 'castellum'. Significat autem divitias spirituales et virtutem quae urbe munita praesidiumque habet. In traditione Christiana, nomen hoc refertur ad divitias animae et protectionem divinam.

in_english.name: Milburga
in_english.meaning: Strong and wealthy, a fortified city or rich fortress
in_english.long_meaning: The name Milburga originates from Old English, derived from 'mil' meaning 'wealth' and 'burg' meaning 'fortress' or 'fortified city'. It symbolizes spiritual wealth combined with the strength and protection offered by a fortified structure. Historically, the name has been associated with Christian virtues of inner richness and spiritual fortitude. Milburga is a name that reflects a strong and wealthy spiritual presence, embodying both material and spiritual prosperity.

celebrity_usage: Milburga the saint, daughter of Saint Wulfhere, was a seventh-century English princess and abbess.

saint_reference.note: Saint Milburga was an Anglo-Saxon nun and abbess, known for her piety and the founding of a monastery.

data.cultural_impact: In medieval Europe, Milburga was venerated as a Christian saint. Many churches were built in her honor, and her feast day was celebrated on the 17th of November. Milburga was believed to have had the power to heal numerous ailments, particularly those related to iron or sword wounds. Devotees would travel great distances to visit her shrines, seeking her intercession and healing grace. Milk, as a symbol of purity, nourishment, and protection, was frequently associated with Milburga and played a significant role in her cult.
data.spiritual_significance: Milburga's name embodies the Christian virtues of healing, protection, and nourishment. For those undergoing physical or emotional pain, her name echoes the comfort and relief found in the healing properties of milk. It also serves as a reminder of the spiritual fortress—the unwavering presence of God—that protects and nourishes us during times of hardship. The name Milburga invites us to lean on our faith during difficult moments, seeking strength and solace in both God's healing power and the communal support of the Church.
